title: One operator, one index, exchanging records with peers
description: One administration running its own index, which pulls from peers it names or finds from their adverts, every native rule enforced. It exchanges records; it claims nothing about independent replication, however many peers it has, which only federated-operators@1 can claim once independently administered operators have been observed.

admission.nativeRules: As single-operator@1. A state or anchor a peer offers is admitted under this index's own publisher policy, anchoring settings and custody policy, exactly as if it had been announced to it; a peer's admission decides nothing here.

publisherPolicy.keySet: Publisher identity keys are configured explicitly (SERVICE_IDENTITY_KEY or a signed publisher policy, ANCHOR_SERVICE_KEYS), never derived from the operator's own key or from a peer, and named in the capability document.
publisherPolicy.historicalAuthorisation: A state's publisher signature is verified against a key that was authorised at the state's time; the current allowlist alone is not authority for a historical state.
publisherPolicy.handover: A publisher handover is a signed authorisation record under the selected governance policy with the old key's evidence preserved; it never moves a token spending key, which only the custody mechanism can move.

discovery.notes: Peers come from SHIP adverts found through SLAP trackers, from a static list the operator names, or both; the capability document says which. Discovery says where records may be found: it never authorises a publisher, and a discovered peer is asked for nothing its capability document shows this index could not admit.

synchronisation.deduplication: Admission of a held outpoint is a no-op; an anchor is deduplicated by outpoint and digest.
synchronisation.proofUpdates: Proofs arrive through POST /arc-ingest or with a synchronised state, are validated against the header source before storage and never replay held outputs.
synchronisation.checkpoints: A checkpoint per peer and topic, held at an offered output that did not arrive so the next round offers it again; an output left behind is asked for again after a back-off.
synchronisation.bounds: Request body 8 MiB, lookup 500 outputs, anchor page 100 default and 500 maximum, at most a configured number of discovered peers a round, and back-off for a peer that cannot be read.
synchronisation.reorganisation: A proof the header source refutes returns the state to pending until repaired.

retention.spentStates: Spent passport states are retained as history through coinsToRetain, whether announced or synchronised.
retention.anchorLeaves: Anchor outputs are retained and indexed; eviction follows the engine's rules.
retention.bytes: Every admitted transaction's BEEF is stored once per transaction.

mustDeclare: synchronisation.profile single-operator@2 with discovery, gasp and peers

acceptance.exercise: Pull both rails from a named peer and serve the same transactions and merkle paths; a second round admits nothing new.
Pull both rails from a peer a discovery plan found rather than one the operator named, through the same engine path.
Refuse a state a peer offers that is signed by a key outside this index's policy, and log the refusal.
Hold the checkpoint at an offered output that did not arrive, leave it behind after the configured rounds, and ask for it again after the back-off.
Serve a capability document that validates against the schema and names single-operator@2 with its discovery mode and peers.

unsupported.reason: One administration cannot claim independently replicated evidence, however many peers it exchanges records with.
